context: A community centre coordinator gives a talk introducing the centre's facilities and layout to new visitors.

lines.text: Now turn to Section Two. You will hear a talk given by a coordinator at a community centre.

Now listen and answer questions eleven to fifteen.
Good evening, everyone, and welcome to Elmwood Community Centre. I'm Olivia, one of the coordinators here, and I'll give you a quick overview of what we offer.
We're open Monday to Friday from eight in the morning until nine in the evening.
At weekends, we close a little earlier, at six pm, on both Saturday and Sunday.
Membership itself is free for local residents, though a few of our specialist classes do carry a small charge — pottery, for instance, is twelve dollars a session.
If you're interested in volunteering, that's coordinated separately, through Marcus, who you can reach directly on extension two-oh-four.
We also hold a Summer Fete out in the garden every June, which tends to be very popular with local families.
Questions sixteen to twenty. Label the plan below. Write the correct letter, A to H, next to questions sixteen to twenty. First, you have some time to look at questions sixteen to twenty.
Now listen and answer questions sixteen to twenty.
Now, let me quickly talk you through the building itself, since it's easy to get a little lost on your first visit.
As you come in through the main entrance, the reception desk is straight ahead of you — that's always the first stop, so we can sign you in.
To the left of reception, along the corridor, you'll find the Oak Room, which is our largest space — mainly used for fitness classes and bigger gatherings.
If you carry on to the far end of that same corridor, on the right-hand side, that's the Willow Room, which is smaller, and where we run most of our art and craft sessions.
Just below the Willow Room, at the back of the building, is the Reading Room — that one's kept quiet, and it's reserved for study groups and our book club.
And finally, directly opposite the Reading Room, on the other side of the building, you'll find our little café, where you're welcome to grab a tea or coffee before or after a session.
That's everything I wanted to cover tonight. Feel free to take a leaflet on your way out, and thank you all for coming.
That is the end of Section Two. Now turn to Section Three.
